resources.string: UPM Mail is an independent, unofficial email client published by zango, with source code in the pportilla/simple_webmail_upm GitHub project. It connects to an existing mailbox; it does not create a developer or university account. This policy describes the data handled by this app.

Before mailbox setup, the app asks for a date of birth to determine an age group. Only the group is retained; the birth date is not stored or transmitted. Users under 18 use supervised mail. Mailbox access stays blocked until setup is complete. An adult completes local setup, reads the data notice and creates a guardian PIN before mailbox credentials can be used. The app keeps the selected age group, PIN verification data, supervision settings, approved or blocked addresses, message approvals and requests for guardian review on this device. The adult birth date entered during setup is checked locally and is not retained or sent to a server. Requests for guardian review remain local and are not automatically sent to zango or the provider. An adult can separately compose a provider report, choose its destination and approve the exact text before transmission through the mail server. The report also includes the sending account identity and normal email headers; original messages and attachments are not automatically included. The PIN controls this app; it does not independently verify identity, parental authority or legal consent.\n\nSupervised mail shows plain text that a guardian has reviewed, and sending requires guardian approval of the exact message and recipients. Supervised drafts stay on the device until an approved send. Device-contact import, attachments, remote resources, external links, exports and search are unavailable in the supervised interface. An adult manages contacts, reviews messages and can disable sending or revoke access. These controls do not change the mail provider\'s account eligibility, data practices or server-side records. A guardian must choose an account the child is permitted to use.

The app uses your email address, login name and password to connect directly to the IMAP and SMTP servers you configure. It downloads mail and sends messages, recipients, your sender name and selected attachments through those servers. Saved drafts, mail changes and server search terms are also sent to your provider when those features are used. Connections require TLS with certificate and hostname verification. TLS protects the connection; email is not end-to-end encrypted by this app. Your provider and message recipients handle their copies under their own policies.

Account settings, cached messages, a search index, recent searches, address history, drafts, queued messages and downloaded or selected attachments are stored in the app\'s private storage. Passwords are encrypted using a key in Android Keystore. The mailbox database and attachment files are not separately encrypted by the app; they rely on Android\'s storage protections. App backup and device transfer are disabled. The app has no advertising, analytics or automatic crash-reporting service, and no developer-operated mail relay.

In the standard mail interface, if you grant Contacts permission, the app reads matching names and email addresses on your device to suggest recipients. It does not upload your address book. A contact you select becomes part of a draft or message and is sent to the mail server when that draft is saved remotely or the message is sent. You can deny or revoke Contacts permission in Android settings and type addresses yourself. Supervised mail uses guardian-approved addresses instead of importing device contacts.

In the standard mail interface, remote content is blocked by default. If you allow it for a message, a trusted sender or all mail, the app contacts the content hosts. They receive your IP address and requested resource URL, which may identify a message or reveal that it was opened. You can change image settings and forget trusted senders in Settings. Links you open are handled by your browser or another selected app, whose privacy practices apply. Supervised messages are displayed as plain text without loading remote resources or opening links.

In the standard mail interface, files you choose in the system picker or share into UPM Mail are copied into private app storage for composing mail. When you open, share, save or print a message or attachment, the selected app, destination or print service receives the content needed for that action. Exported copies are outside this app\'s control. These attachment, sharing and export actions are unavailable in the supervised interface.

Mail checks and the instant-mail service contact your configured servers while the app is in the background. Instant mail is off by default. If you select Instantly (push), it keeps an IMAP connection open and shows an ongoing notification. To stop it in the standard interface, change Settings → Check for new mail to a periodic interval or Only when I open the app. Standard mail notifications can show sender names, subjects and previews, including on the lock screen depending on Android settings. Supervised mail uses periodic or manual checks, not instant push, and does not show mail-content notifications. You control notifications and background access in the app and Android settings.

Cached mail may be trimmed and downloaded again. Drafts and queued messages remain until sent or removed. To disconnect a mailbox, open Settings, choose the account and remove it. This deletes its saved password, local mail records and associated private attachment copies. Shared address history and recent searches are cleared when the last account is removed. Global settings, age group, guardian PIN verification data, approved or blocked contacts and local review requests may remain. An adult can resolve review requests in the app. Clear app storage in Android settings or uninstall to remove the remaining private app data. Files you exported and copies held by mail servers or recipients remain. Removing an account from this app does not delete the university or provider account; contact your provider for that request.

For privacy questions, contact zango at p.portilla89@gmail.com. Your inquiry is handled to respond to your request; do not send passwords or unnecessary private message content. This policy will be updated when the app\'s data handling changes.
